Every command of the `goal` CLI, in the order its usage text lists them: each section shows the command's forms, what it does and its flags. `goal` without a valid command prints the same text and exits 2.

## Conventions

&lt;item&gt; is goal#2, the item's id, or a bare number.

--move S=T sends the open items of station S to station T.

## goal up

```text
goal up [--compose]
```

start it; --compose runs goald as compose services too

Flags: `--compose`.

## goal answer

```text
goal answer <item> "<text>" | --choice <n>
```

answer the question in your words

Flags: `--choice <n>`.

## goal factory push

```text
goal factory push <dir> [--publish [--message M]] [--force] [--move S=T]...
```

make the folder the \*draft\*

Flags: `--publish`, `--message M`, `--force`, `--move S=T`.

## goal factory restore

```text
goal factory restore <factory> <N> [--move S=T]...
goal factory restore <factory>
```

run version N again

list an archived factory again

Flags: `--move S=T`.

## goal triggers show

```text
goal triggers show <factory> <trigger> [--json]
```

a trigger and its items

Flags: `--json`.
